evidence.quote: A 48-year-old man
A 48-year-old man
with gastric cancer was scheduled for laparoscopic gastrectomy
He was on maintenance dialysis for chronic renal failure.
He had been on hemodialysis for chronic renal failure.

facts.clinical_statement: Chronic renal failure on maintenance dialysis

evidence.quote: His medical history included coronary artery bypass grafting for angina.
Blood tests were done a day before surgery and prior to maintenance hemodialysis showed mild hyperkalemia (serum K^(+) 5.4 mEq/L).

facts.clinical_statement: Mild hyperkalemia on preoperative blood tests

evidence.quote: An hour into surgery, his arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis showed hyperkalemia serum K^(+) =6.3 mEq/L (Table 1).
This is the first report of severe intraoperative hyperkalemia due to retraction-related hepatic infarction during LG.

facts.clinical_statement: Severe intraoperative hyperkalemia first detected an hour into surgery
facts.notes: Severity from the authors' own statement; the causal link to hepatic infarction is the authors' hypothesis (see ambiguities).

evidence.quote: Emergent computed tomography (CT) showed a low-density area in the left lobe of the liver (Fig. 2), suggestive of hepatic infarction.

facts.notes: Text and Fig. 2 caption say CT is suggestive of/suggesting infarction; abstract and title state it as established. Kept provisional.

evidence.quote: suggestive of liver damage, most probably due to intraoperative liver retraction
We initiated glycyrrhizin infusion for suspected liver damage.

facts.notes: Cause is hedged ("most probably"); not recorded as an attribute.

evidence.quote: Treatment with antibiotic agent was initiated for presumed infection of the infarcted liver.

facts.clinical_statement: Presumed infection of the infarcted liver

evidence.quote: due to a slowly developing subcapsular hematoma []. In our case, the postoperative CT showed no such hematoma.

facts.clinical_statement: No subcapsular hematoma on postoperative CT

evidence.quote: with gastric cancer was scheduled for laparoscopic gastrectomy

facts.notes: Alternate representation of the gastric cancer condition.

evidence.quote: A 48-year-old man underwent laparoscopic gastrectomy for gastric cancer.

facts.notes: Alternate representation of the gastrectomy procedure.

we induced general anesthesia by intravenous administration of propofol 60 mg, fentanyl 100 μg, and rocuronium 70 mg

Bolus 1.5% lidocaine epidural infusion and intravenous fentanyl infusion were added as needed.

summary.text: A 48-year-old man on maintenance hemodialysis for chronic renal failure, with a history of coronary bypass for angina, was scheduled for laparoscopic gastrectomy for gastric cancer. Blood tests the day before surgery, before hemodialysis, showed mild hyperkalemia with serum potassium 5.4 mEq/L, and potassium was not rechecked after dialysis.

Surgery was done in the reverse Trendelenburg position with the enlarged liver retracted. An hour into surgery arterial blood gas analysis showed serum potassium 6.3 mEq/L while only potassium-free infusion had been given, and the cause was unclear at that point. Potassium kept rising despite treatment, with a maximum of 7.4 mEq/L during surgery.

A glucose-insulin infusion was started and increased gradually, and sodium bicarbonate was given during the fifth hour. After surgery AST and ALT rose markedly, glycyrrhizin was started for suspected liver damage, emergency hemodialysis was avoided, hemodialysis resumed on POD 1 and continuous hemodiafiltration ran from POD 1 to POD 4.

On POD 5 the patient developed a fever of 39 °C, and emergent CT showed a low-density area in the liver suggestive of hepatic infarction. Antibiotics were started for presumed infection of the infarcted liver, the patient responded well, and he was discharged 27 days after surgery.
